We are a team of Mechatronics Engineers, Computer Scientists and Mathematicians with hands-on experience in rocket avionics, rover simulations, drones and volunteer initiatives.

For this challange, we are tackling "Flame in Freefall".  :-)
summary:
For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, we developed Şule-i Feza, an interactive, data-driven web dashboard designed to analyze and visualize microgravity combustion and spacecraft fire-safety data.What we developed:
We built an application that aggregates and processes hundreds of thousands of rows from NASA Physical Science Informatics (PSI) datasets (such as BASS, ACME, and SAFFIRE). The platform models critical combustion metrics including burn duration, pressure, oxygen concentration, and droplet diameter squared decay ($$(D/D_0)^2$$) across various fuel parameters like $n$-dodecane.How it addresses the challenge:
The dashboard transforms complex, hard-to-navigate aerospace experimental data into intuitive visualizations and actionable insights, enabling researchers and engineers to rapidly interpret flame behavior in freefall environments.Why it is important:
As human spaceflight expands toward the Moon and Mars, understanding fire dynamics in microgravity is vital for spacecraft safety and life-support system design. Our project bridges raw NASA open data with practical, high-performance web tooling to enhance future mission safety.
details:
What it does and how it works: Şule-i Feza is an interactive, data-driven web platform designed to process, analyze, and visualize complex aerospace and combustion data. It aggregates hundreds of thousands of rows from NASA Physical Science Informatics (PSI) datasets (including BASS, BASS-II, ACME, SAFFIRE, SLICE, SPICE, CFI, and SAME-R) to model crucial parameters such as burn duration, oxygen concentration, pressure, and droplet diameter squared decay ((D/D_0)^2) across fuel types like $n$-dodecane.

Benefits and Intended Impact: As human space exploration scales toward the Moon and Mars, understanding fire dynamics in microgravity is critical for crew survival and spacecraft life-support engineering. Our project transforms raw, hard-to-navigate experimental telemetry into clear, actionable visualizations, bridging the gap between open-source NASA science and practical aerospace safety insights.

Tools, Languages, and Technologies: The platform was developed using Python (Flask, pandas, numpy, openpyxl) for backend data processing and statistical aggregation, combined with a responsive HTML and JavaScript (Fetch API) frontend interface to deliver real-time, interactive data visualizations.

Creativity and Considerations: The project creatively solves the challenge of massive data overload by turning hundreds of thousands of dense experimental records into an intuitive, high-performance web dashboard. Our team prioritized user experience, data integrity, and cross-platform accessibility to ensure researchers and space enthusiasts alike can effortlessly interpret complex microgravity combustion phenomena.
